newsitem.title: CHINA: China military zone recovers 787 improper homes.
newsitem.headline: China military zone recovers 787 improper homes.

text.p: China has taken back 787 overly large homes occupied by officers of the Beijing Military Region, and punished 17 people, in a drive to improve honesty in the military, the People's Liberation Army Daily said on Monday.

"The Communist Party Committee of the Beijing Military Region has seized on the return of excessively large homes of leaders and cadres as a major part of strengthening the party work style and of construction of an honest government," the newspaper said.

The military region had so far disciplined 17 division-level officials and ordered various army units to take action against officers whose housing exceeded the limits on army housing rules, the newspaper said.
The People's Liberation Army has rules on the size of housing allocated to various ranks, but many officers use their rank to obtain roomier living space or several homes.

After the military region launched a drive against violating military housing regulations, more than 30 officers at or above the division level had turned over improperly large homes, it said but did not specify how many homes.
Officials from the military region's command, political and logistics departments had followed suit and turned over 202 houses, the newspaper said. These were included among the 787 homes.
Authorities would not be lenient on those caught trying to evade the regulations, it said.
"Those who don't rectify their mistakes will not be shielded...and party committees at every level will adopt decisive measures to deal with them," it said.
Names of offenders would be made public and authorities would set up a hotline and letter box for complaints against those suspected of violating housing rules, it said.
China has vowed to crack down on abuses of official power and graft, warning that corruption is a virus that threatens to undermine Communist Party rule.
